question: Does one already-existing causal variable explain H12 directional-edge failure consistently across chronological selection folds without reusing a rejected mechanism?
selection_rule: first 70% of decision timestamps within each outer fold, identical chronological boundary semantics to split_selection_evaluation

interpretation.lag_return_1h: weak same-sign association in all three selection folds, but not materially new: recent/lagged return information is already represented in H12 and lag_return_1h was already used in prior H4/H8 research controls/inputs
interpretation.other_same_sign_raw_features: realized volatility, activity/volume, taker imbalance and funding show weak same-sign associations but are already direct H12 factor columns and/or prior rejected reliability families
interpretation.categorical_states: trend/funding/session/exposure/vol/activity state means do not provide a consistent state-specific directional rescue across all folds
